body.statement: If \(\tau_n=n\rho_n\to\infty\) and \(\Lambda_{\ell n}\to\lambda_{\ell}\in\mathbb R\), then jointly over \(1\le\ell\le L\), \((\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}-\Delta_{\ell})/\sqrt{\rho_nV_{\ell}/n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\) and \((\widehat\Delta^P_{\ell}-\Delta_{\ell})/\sqrt{\rho_nV_{\ell}/n}\Rightarrow N(Q_{\ell}\lambda_{\ell}/\sqrt{V_{\ell}},1)\), with independent coordinates. Moreover, the exact-link and Poisson-ratio estimators are first-order equivalent for pair \(\ell\) if and only if \(\Lambda_{\ell n}\to0\).
body.justification: The result turns link disagreement into a drifting noncentrality parameter rather than an informal approximation error.
body.gap: Djuazon and Tsyawo give only interior Gaussian weak convergence, while Chen and Fang do not allow the base cell probabilities to vanish.
body.consumer: A distributional-DiD analyst can determine whether a Poisson shortcut changes first-order inference for each pre/post comparison.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a pair \(\ell\), suppress its index, and write \(a_n=(\rho_n/n)^{1/2}\).  The add-half estimator satisfies the exact decomposition
\[
\widetilde r_j-r_j
=\frac{K_j-n_jr_j}{n_j+1}+\frac{1/2-r_j}{n_j+1}.
\tag{1}
\]
The second term is \(O(n^{-1})=o(a_n)\), because \(n\rho_n\to\infty\) and the role shares are bounded below.  For fixed real \(t_1,\ldots,t_4\), expansion of the logarithm of the characteristic function of the independent centered Bernoulli sums in (1) gives
\[
\log\mathbb E\exp\left\{i\sum_{j=1}^4t_j\sqrt{\frac n{\rho_n}}
\frac{K_j-n_jr_j}{n_j+1}\right\}
=-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^4t_j^2\frac{c_j}{\pi_j}+o(1).
\]
Indeed, the quadratic term is the displayed limit, while the sum of absolute third-order terms is bounded by a constant times \((n\rho_n)^{-1/2}\); the maximal normalized summand has the same order.  Thus
\[
\sqrt{\frac n{\rho_n}}(\widetilde r-r)
\ \Rightarrow\ N\!\left(0,\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{c_1}{\pi_1},\ldots,\frac{c_4}{\pi_4}\right)\right).
\tag{2}
\]
The same calculation for the fixed sixty cells and mutual independence gives joint convergence with independent pair coordinates.

For \(P(p)=p_1p_2/p_3-p_4\),
\[
\nabla P(r)=\left(\frac{c_2}{c_3},\frac{c_1}{c_3},-\frac{c_1c_2}{c_3^2},-1\right).
\tag{3}
\]
On the event \(\max_j|\widetilde r_j/r_j-1|\le1/2\), whose probability tends to one by (1) and \(n\rho_n\to\infty\), the Hessian of \(P\) is \(O(\rho_n^{-1})\).  Hence its Taylor remainder is
\[
O_P\!\left(\rho_n^{-1}\|\widetilde r-r\|^2\right)=O_P(n^{-1})=o_P(a_n).
\]
Combining (2)--(3) gives
\[
\frac{\widehat\Delta^P-\Delta^P}{\sqrt{\rho_nV/n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
\tag{4}
\]
because the variance obtained from (2)--(3) is
\[
\frac{c_4}{\pi_4}
+\frac{Q^2}{\pi_1c_1}+\frac{Q^2}{\pi_2c_2}+\frac{Q^2}{\pi_3c_3}=V>0.
\]

We next treat the exact map directly, rather than differentiating an asymptotic error formula.  If \(s=q(p_1)+q(p_2)-q(p_3)\) and \(e=(1,1,-1)\), then
\[
H_j(p)=e_j\frac{\phi(s)}{\phi(q(p_j))},
\]
and
\[
H_{jk}(p)=H_j(p)\left\{-\frac{s e_k}{\phi(q(p_k))}
+\mathbf1\{j=k\}\frac{q(p_j)}{\phi(q(p_j))}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Repeating the quantile-shift and Mills-remainder estimates from the common-cutoff proof on the fixed compact coefficient interval \([1/4,6]\) (their derivation uses only positivity and finite compact endpoints) gives, uniformly on the preceding high-probability neighborhood,
\[
H(r)=\rho_nQ\{1+O(u_n^{-2})\},\qquad
\frac{m(s)}{m(q(r_j))}=1+O(u_n^{-2}).
\]
Since \(\phi(v)=\Phi(v)m(v)\), (5) consequently gives
\[
\nabla\{H(p_1,p_2,p_3)-p_4\}\big|_{p=r}
=\nabla P(r)+O(u_n^{-2}).
\tag{6}
\]
Also (5), \(|s|+|q(r_j)|=O(u_n)\), and \(\phi(q(r_j))=r_jm(q(r_j))\asymp\rho_nu_n\) show that the exact-map Hessian is \(O(\rho_n^{-1})\) on the same high-probability neighborhood.  Its Taylor remainder is therefore again \(o_P(a_n)\).  Equations (2), (5), and (6) prove
\[
\frac{\widehat\Delta^E-\Delta}{\sqrt{\rho_nV/n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{7}
\]

The exact factorization and the uniform coefficient theorem give, without an additive error that could dominate near a cancellation plane,
\[
\frac{\Delta^P-\Delta}{\sqrt{\rho_nV/n}}
=\frac{Q}{\sqrt V}\frac{A\sqrt{n\rho_n}}{u_n^2}
\{1+O(u_n^{-2})\}
=\frac{Q}{\sqrt V}\Lambda_n\{1+O(u_n^{-2})\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus, if \(\Lambda_n\to\lambda\), adding (8) to (4) gives the asserted noncentral normal limit.  The coefficient limits imply \(Q_n/\sqrt{V_n}\to Q/\sqrt V\in(0,\infty)\).  Subtracting the Taylor expansions behind (4) and (7) also gives
\[
\frac{\widehat\Delta^P-\widehat\Delta^E}{\sqrt{\rho_nV/n}}
=\frac{Q}{\sqrt V}\Lambda_n\{1+o(1)\}+o_P(1).
\]
Consequently the two estimators differ by \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n/n})\) if and only if \(\Lambda_n\to0\).  Repeating the argument over the fixed set of \(L\) pairs proves the stated joint limits and independence.
